sources.provider: OpenAQ v3, upstream provider CPCB (Central Pollution Control Board monitoring network)
sources.official_dataset_name: OpenAQ sensor hourly aggregates for CPCB-network monitors
sources.units: ug/m3 (gas sensors reporting ppb are not converted to mass)
sources.sampling_frequency: hourly aggregates; daily station targets derived by AirGuard
sources.license: OpenAQ terms; per-station upstream licence metadata preserved (docs/LICENSES.md)
sources.update_frequency: as delivered by OpenAQ; its CPCB copy stopped advancing on 2026-10-07 14:30 UTC (observed 2026-10-09)
sources.quality_control: 75% hourly coverage, provider flags, zero readings, stuck-sensor runs, invalid values; Severe days kept as lower-bound censored targets
sources.issue_time_availability: OpenAQ healthy-feed latency <= 3 hours; historical publication time is NOT observed
sources.note: OpenAQ CPCB provider; AirGuard CPCB-style targets, not official bulletin AQI

sources.official_dataset_name: Real time Air Quality Index from various locations

sources.issue_time_availability: Each value was forecast by a run initialised at least 48 hours before its valid hour. Every hour of a target day therefore comes from a run initialised before the 20:00 IST issue time of the previous day. This is older than the forecast an operator would have had, so it handicaps the weather features rather than flattering them.
sources.not_available: boundary_layer_height is not archived at any previous-run lead (verified: all null).
sources.license: Open-Meteo CC BY 4.0; free API non-commercial

sources.provider: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (ECMWF), via the Atmosphere Data Store
sources.product: 00 UTC operational forecast, surface and lowest model level, 0.4-degree grid
sources.license: Copernicus licence (free; attribution 'Generated using Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service information')

sources.official_dataset_name: Open-Meteo Air Quality API, past hours
sources.issue_time_availability: The provider archives fields for past hours without the run that produced them and does not serve earlier runs for air quality. Values for a target day come from runs initialised at or after the 20:00 IST issue time. This is a short-lead proxy for the forecast that would have been available, and it must never be described as that forecast.
sources.use: exploratory only; never a substitute for archived operational forecasts
sources.license: Open-Meteo CC BY 4.0 + Copernicus attribution; free API non-commercial

sources.provider: OpenAQ locations, with versioned AirGuard corrections
sources.note: Coordinates and city labels as delivered, corrected only through versioned correction files; current-catalogue survivorship is a disclosed limitation

sources.upstream: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India
sources.use: 1.0 historical replay only; cannot establish today's conditions or forecast availability

sources.provider: Open-Meteo (CAMS global air quality, GFS weather), OpenAQ, NASA FIRMS
sources.label_on_site: MODELLED unless a recent nearby station supplies MEASURED values

sources.rule: issued forecasts are append-only; outcomes are paired later and never alter the issued value
evidence: database: airguard.forecast_runs / research_forecast_runs and their verification tables

sources.issue_time_availability: Near-real-time detections carry acquisition date and time. The issue-time cutoff, with a three-hour processing allowance, is applied to each detection when features are built.
sources.research_use: WITHHELD: acquisition time alone does not prove publication time
sources.license: NASA open data policy; FIRMS attribution
